title.en: The First World War, and votes for women
title.fr: La Première Guerre mondiale et le droit de vote des femmes

text.en: Canada was part of the British Empire, and most Canadians were proud of that.
text.fr: Le Canada faisait partie de l'Empire britannique, et la plupart des Canadiens en étaient fiers.

source.quote: Most Canadians were proud to be part of the British Empire.

verification.evidence: Most Canadians were proud to be part of the British Empire.

text.en: In 1900 Canadians fought in two battles in South Africa, Paardeberg and Lillefontein. Both were won, and both made Canadians prouder of their country.
text.fr: En 1900, des Canadiens ont pris part à deux batailles en Afrique du Sud, Paardeberg et Lillefontein. Ces victoires ont renforcé la fierté nationale au Canada.

source.quote: In 1900, Canadians took part in the battles of Paardeberg (“Horse Mountain”) and Lillefontein, victories that strengthened national pride in Canada.

verification.evidence: In 1900, Canadians took part in the battles of Paardeberg (“Horse Mountain”) and Lillefontein, victories that strengthened national pride in Canada.

text.en: Germany attacked Belgium and France in 1914 and Britain declared war. Ottawa then raised the Canadian Expeditionary Force, which later became the Canadian Corps.
text.fr: L'Allemagne a attaqué la Belgique et la France en 1914 et la Grande-Bretagne a déclaré la guerre. Ottawa a alors formé le Corps expéditionnaire canadien, qui est devenu plus tard le Corps canadien.

source.quote: When Germany attacked Belgium and France in 1914 and Britain declared war, Ottawa formed the Canadian Expeditionary Force (later the Canadian Corps).

verification.evidence: When Germany attacked Belgium and France in 1914 and Britain declared war, Ottawa formed the Canadian Expeditionary Force (later the Canadian Corps).

text.en: Vimy made the Canadians' name as soldiers. Their courage earned them a reputation as the British Empire's shock troops.
text.fr: Vimy a fait la réputation des soldats canadiens. Leur courage leur a valu d'être vus comme les troupes de choc de l'Empire britannique.

source.quote: securing the Canadians’ reputation for valour as the “shock troops of the British Empire.”

verification.evidence: The Canadian Corps captured Vimy Ridge in April 1917, with 10,000 killed or wounded, securing the Canadians’ reputation for valour as the “shock troops of the British Empire.”

text.en: That battle has its own day of remembrance. April 9 is Vimy Day.
text.fr: Cette bataille a sa propre journée du souvenir. Le 9 avril est le jour de Vimy.

source.quote: April 9 is celebrated as Vimy Day.

verification.evidence: April 9 is celebrated as Vimy Day.

text.en: One Canadian officer described what he saw at Vimy. He said the whole country, from one ocean to the other, was on parade, and that in those few minutes he watched a nation begin.
text.fr: Un officier canadien a décrit ce qu'il a vu à Vimy. Il a dit que tout le pays, d'un océan à l'autre, était au défilé et que, en quelques minutes, il avait vu naître une nation.

source.quote: One Canadian officer said: “It was Canada from the Atlantic to the Pacific on parade

verification.evidence: One Canadian officer said: “It was Canada from the Atlantic to the Pacific on parade … In those few minutes I witnessed the birth of a nation.”

text.en: Britain advised Ottawa against the internment policy. Canada went ahead with it anyway.
text.fr: La Grande-Bretagne a déconseillé à Ottawa la politique d'internement. Le Canada l'a tout de même appliquée.

source.quote: even though Britain advised against the policy.

verification.evidence: Regrettably, from 1914 to 1920, Ottawa interned over 8,000 former Austro-Hungarian subjects, mainly Ukrainian men, as “enemy aliens” in 24 labour camps across Canada, even though Britain advised against the policy.

text.en: In the last hundred days of the war, the Canadian Corps pushed forward. It advanced beside French and British Empire troops.
text.fr: Pendant les cent derniers jours de la guerre, le Corps canadien a mené l'offensive. Il progressait aux côtés des troupes françaises et de celles de l'Empire britannique.

source.quote: the Canadian Corps advanced alongside the French and British Empire troops in the last hundred days

verification.evidence: In 1918, under the command of General Sir Arthur Currie, Canada’s greatest soldier, the Canadian Corps advanced alongside the French and British Empire troops in the last hundred days.

text.en: The Canadians won at Amiens on August 8, 1918, a day the German army itself called black. Victories at Arras, Canal du Nord, Cambrai and Mons followed.
text.fr: Les Canadiens ont vaincu à Amiens le 8 août 1918, une journée que l'armée allemande elle-même a qualifiée de noire. D'autres victoires ont suivi à Arras, au canal du Nord, à Cambrai et à Mons.

source.quote: These included the victorious Battle of Amiens on August 8, 1918—which the Germans called “the black day of the German Army”—followed by Arras, Canal du Nord, Cambrai and Mons.

verification.evidence: These included the victorious Battle of Amiens on August 8, 1918—which the Germans called “the black day of the German Army”—followed by Arras, Canal du Nord, Cambrai and Mons.

text.en: The war left Canadians prouder both of their own country and of the Empire. That feeling was strongest in English Canada.
text.fr: La guerre a accru la fierté des Canadiens envers leur pays et envers l'Empire. Ce sentiment était le plus fort au Canada anglais.

source.quote: The war strengthened both national and imperial pride, particularly in English Canada.

verification.evidence: The war strengthened both national and imperial pride, particularly in English Canada.

text.en: Women had to fight for the right to vote. That long effort is called the women's suffrage movement.
text.fr: Les femmes ont dû lutter pour obtenir le droit de vote. On appelle ce long combat le mouvement pour le suffrage des femmes.

source.quote: The effort by women to achieve the right to vote is known as the women’s suffrage movement.

verification.evidence: The effort by women to achieve the right to vote is known as the women’s suffrage movement.

text.en: Canada was not unusual in limiting who could vote. Most democracies of that time did the same.
text.fr: Le Canada n'était pas une exception en limitant le droit de vote. La plupart des démocraties de l'époque faisaient de même.

source.quote: This was common in most democratic countries at the time.

verification.evidence: At the time of Confederation, the vote was limited to property-owning adult white males. This was common in most democratic countries at the time.

text.en: In 1917 the government of Sir Robert Borden opened the federal vote to some women. Nurses serving at the front could vote first, then women with a close relative in active service.
text.fr: En 1917, le gouvernement de sir Robert Borden a accordé le vote fédéral à certaines femmes. Les infirmières servant au front ont voté les premières, puis les femmes ayant un proche en service actif.

source.quote: the federal government of Sir Robert Borden gave women the right to vote in federal elections—first to nurses at the battle front, then to women who were related to men in active wartime service.

verification.evidence: In 1917, thanks to the leadership of women such as Dr. Stowe and other suffragettes, the federal government of Sir Robert Borden gave women the right to vote in federal elections—first to nurses at the battle front, then to women who were related to men in active wartime service.

text.en: Remembrance Day honours more than a million men and women who have served Canada. It also honours the 110,000 who died.
text.fr: Le jour du Souvenir honore plus d'un million d'hommes et de femmes qui ont servi le Canada. Il honore aussi les 110 000 qui ont donné leur vie.

source.quote: to honour the sacrifices of over a million brave men and women who have served, and the 110,000 who have given their lives.

verification.evidence: Canadians wear the red poppy and observe a moment of silence at the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month to honour the sacrifices of over a million brave men and women who have served, and the 110,000 who have given their lives.

text.en: The poem written by John McCrae is still read aloud at ceremonies on Remembrance Day.
text.fr: Le poème écrit par John McCrae est encore récité lors des cérémonies du jour du Souvenir.

source.quote: it is often recited on Remembrance Day

verification.evidence: Canadian medical officer Lieutenant Colonel John McCrae composed the poem “In Flanders Fields” in 1915; it is often recited on Remembrance Day
